newsitem.title: FRANCE: PRESS DIGEST - France - Jan 10. [CORRECTED 10:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - France - Jan 10. [CORRECTED 10:55 GMT]

text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Societe Generale to buy controlling share in Paribas subsidiary Credit du Nord for 2.2 billion francs. Societe Generale plans a 2.5 billion francs capital increase to bring Credit du Nord's tier one capital ratio in line with Societe Generale standards. Paribas to concentrate on core investment banking activity. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, L'Agefi, Liberation, The International Herald Tribune).
-- Chancellor Helmut Kohl calls for Germany to unite to fight unemployment.
-- Four unions at France Telecom sign agreement on youth apprenticeships and flexibility of working hours that includes opening branch offices on Saturdays.
-- Jean Peyrelevade, chairman of ailing state-owned bank Credit Lyonnais, is to present a bailout plan to EU authorities in Brussels on Monday (corrects from Tuesday).
-- Credit Lyonnais is expected to report heavy losses linked to the sale of its European subsidiaries, estimated up to nine billion francs.
-- Forecasts by Centre de Prevision de l'Expansion sees 1997 French PIB growth at 2 percent, Credit Lyonnais at 1.9 percent.
-- National statistics office's monthly household survey shows slight improvement in perceptions of living standards and employment expectations.
-- Renault carmaker runs into supply difficulties as its "Megane Scenic" minivan proves an unexpected commercial success. Plant may consider creating night shifts.
-- France Telecom presented highest bid for a 51 percent stake in CI Telecom, Ivory Coast national carrier.
